exact nonlinear count filter described after (1.5). No past control word
must be replayed once this pair has been propagated.

6. WHEN THE FULL CONDITIONAL JOINT STATE IS REQUIRED

future control. With count intensity depending on S, a Bayes update of the

For example, a SWAP transports such a conditional bank by

 r'_0=p_1(1-r_1)/(1-p'_1),                                 (6.1)

when the denominators are positive; null-mode conditionals are arbitrary.

a set of independently driven frozen-mode references. A known flip of S
exchanges its conditional banks. Hidden S jumps require the corresponding
mixture/inflow updates; a controller cannot reset banks at unobserved jumps
using a hidden oracle.

counts, the exact effect module has dimension four. The count multiplier

functions span the full four-point space. Starting at delta_(0,0), the

not additional physical operations. The complete controlled Hankel rank

realize this exact contract linearly; the original two physical bits attain
that positive realization.

not a new general PSR result. It supplies no fixed-error lower bound for
approximate realizations as gamma tends to infinity under a bounded hazard
contract. Such a contract is precisely what the capture pulses violate.

current effective state. A common admitted intervention K writes a binary
persistent coordinate S with different probabilities p and q. Suppose
subsequently S is conserved and the detector is (1.3). Then every common
prediction issued from that effective-state collision incurs worst-case
complete-record error at least

       (|p-q|/2)[exp(-r_-T)-exp(-r_+T)].                    (7.1)

information has entered S. An intervention-sensitive forgetting condition
must therefore control future action effects which transfer discarded
coordinates into retained persistent ones. Relaxation of present readouts
under frozen modes alone does not establish that condition.

capture rate is also gamma, so integrating its influence leaves a constant.

 int a(t) int_{s<t} exp[-gamma*kappa(t-s)] b(s) ds dt,       (7.2)

where b creates unresolved memory and a can convert it into an observed
or persistent coordinate. This displayed expression is a diagnostic form,
not an independently proved general theorem for arbitrary dynamics.

time-ordered action condition could therefore admit some bursts while
excluding the demonstrated capture sequence.

8. ECONOMIC BASELINE: POSITIVE GENERATIVE STATE VERSUS A BELIEF VECTOR

not the cheapest positive GENERATIVE state if microscopic fast event work
is allowed. A simulator can retain one sampled H_U and execute the local
microscopic updates and counts using its own record. Its physical state

contract; it must not be declared free.

A direct consequence of the held theorem gives a safe comparison for this
baseline without falsely conditioning graphical noise on future feedback.
Write F=epsilon^2 Lambda^2 K_k(T),
B=2|epsilon|Lambda T min(1,k m^R), and

it internally samples a hidden physical trajectory.

compresses a conditional predictor, a positive stochastic simulator, or
both. Replacing exponentially many probabilities by a microscopic sample
saves state storage while retaining fast-clock work. A consequential
macroscopic construction should separately explain its mode identification,
initial-data acquisition, kinetics, finite-bit representation, and how its
fast dynamics are propagated without simply paying every microscopic event.
A finite number of real coordinates is not that entire resource argument.

reachable ranks. CAPTURE_EXACT_REPLAY.json preserves its output. The
full-support persistence bound is the analytic coupling proof in Section 4;
the script only verifies its rational margin. Numerical no-event values
are evaluations of the proved expressions, not simulations or measurements.

physical apparatus, or acquired kinetic calibration was used. Existing
native Pro context was inherited without model overrides; exact backend,
token usage and costs are UNKNOWN. This is a bounded constructive
obstruction and repair, not a new mission boundary.

Fast Transient Capture and Retained State Theorem FAST TRANSIENTS CAN BE WRITTEN INTO PERSISTENT PHYSICAL MEMORY
Private Astra P1, 2026-10-24. Producer: /root/predictive_state_obstruction.
No historical novelty, hardware realization or measured advantage is claimed.

SCOPE AND SCIENTIFIC DECISION

A bounded number of interventions, or a bounded integrated transition-rate
budget, does NOT replace a pointwise slow-transition hazard bound in a
partial-forgetting theorem. Two controls at the fast time scale can create
a fast lag and write it into a conserved slow mode. Later finite-rate
observations then have an order-one law discrepancy. Every frozen-mode
fast kernel can still contract at rate gamma, including with full support.

This is not a counterexample to a theorem assuming bounded slow/observed
hazard independent of gamma. It identifies precisely why that assumption
matters and what an intervention-sensitive influence certificate must test.
The example has an economical repair: retain the fast lag during the
capture sequence, or transport the conditional bank through known pulses.
It does not prove the impossibility of compact physical descriptions.

Existing source context read before constructing this example:
 agents/kinetic_predictive_structure_20261024/
 KINETIC_PREDICTIVE_OPERATOR_STRUCTURE.txt;
 DRIVEN_PHYSICAL_MEMORY_UNDER_RAPID_CONTROL_V1.txt;
 LOCAL_LAWS_FROM_SUBCRITICAL_DEPENDENCIES_V1.txt;
 earlier addressable-memory/positive-realization sources were inspected for
 overlap. The existing operator-module result already gives the exact
 intervention-closed state principle. No new claim for PSR rank or controlled
 observability is made here. The new scoped example addresses fast conditional
 relaxation, physical capture and the temporal concentration of kinetic action.

1. COMMON MICROSCOPIC MODEL AND OUTPUT CONTRACT

The physical state is (S,H) in {0,1}^2. S is the retained candidate mode;
H is a fast coordinate. Away from explicitly declared control pulses, S is
conserved and H is reset at rate gamma to a Bernoulli variable of mean

                v_s=eta+(1-2eta)s,  0<=eta<1/2.              (1.1)

Thus conditional on a frozen S=s,

   d E H/dt=gamma(v_s-E H),
   TV(mu exp(t gamma L_s),nu exp(t gamma L_s))
                  =exp(-gamma t) TV(mu,nu).                (1.2)

For 0<eta<1/2 both conditional transition rates are strictly positive.
No common fast equilibrium across modes is assumed. All kernels below
are supplied actual classical kinetic operations, not inferred from an
energy ratio or from passive measurements.

The count detector is OFF during the preparation/control stages. In a
later interval of length T it has intensity

          r_S=lambda[1+epsilon(2S-1)],
          lambda>0, 0<epsilon<1.                           (1.3)

S is conserved during this observation interval. The detector neither
changes S nor H. Its total rate is bounded by lambda(1+epsilon), independent
of gamma. The policies below are open loop and access no hidden state.
Thus they are also admissible members of a feedback policy class.

For a final P(S=1)=p, the entire count-record law is

             P_p=(1-p) P_-+p P_+,                          (1.4)

where P_-/P_+ are homogeneous Poisson path laws at rates
r_-=lambda(1-epsilon),r_+=lambda(1+epsilon). Consequently

 TV(P_p,P_q)=|p-q| TV(P_+,P_-)
 >=|p-q|[exp(-r_- T)-exp(-r_+ T)].                          (1.5)

The equality follows because the signed measure difference is exactly
(p-q)(P_+-P_-). The lower bound uses the no-event event. All discrepancies
below are therefore complete-record discrepancies, not merely differences
in a formally unobserved mean.

We grant the approximate model the EXACT Bayesian filter for its retained
mode S. In particular it produces the mixture (1.4) with its predicted
post-control p, not a single Poisson process at the averaged rate.
For static S, its posterior odds multiply by exp[-(r_+-r_-)dt] during
silence and by r_+/r_- at a count. The failure below persists with this
ordinary nonlinear filtering done correctly.

2. TWO REVERSIBLE SUPPLIED PULSES, WITH FULL-SUPPORT FAST KERNELS

Initially S=0 and H has its conditional stationary law Bernoulli(eta).
For each frozen mode, let the reference bank be rho^s=Bernoulli(v_s).
Its entries are exact conditional stationary distributions and satisfy the
uniform exponential contraction interface (1.2).

At a known time tau apply the reversible permutation

                     (S,H) -> (1-S,H).                     (2.1)

Wait c/gamma, c>0, then apply the reversible SWAP

                     (S,H) -> (H,S).                       (2.2)

No observation is made during either pulse or the intervening wait.
Between the pulses, actual S=1 but actual H starts with mean eta, so

       E H(tau+c/gamma-)=1-eta-(1-2eta)exp(-c).             (2.3)

After SWAP this is the persistent probability P(S=1). An UNTRANSPORTED
bank which substitutes the counterfactual frozen-mode-1 reference rho^1
at the capture step predicts P_hat(S=1)=1-eta. Therefore

             P_hat(S=1)-P(S=1)=(1-2eta)exp(-c).             (2.4)

Equation (1.5) gives a nonvanishing later count-law gap independent of gamma.
For eta=1/4,c=ln2, the mean gap is 1/4. With lambda=T=1,epsilon=1/2,
the no-event gap is (exp(-1/2)-exp(-3/2))/4.

Allowing the unused mode-1 bank a different initial law does not repair
the asymptotic issue: evolving it for the fixed pre-pulse time tau gives
an O(exp(-gamma*tau)) change to its stationary value. What fails is the
absence of TRANSPORT at the actual known mode change, not the choice of
that unused initial reference.

This pair uses actual finite permutation kernels. It does not supply their
laboratory implementation, energetic cost, or finite-duration synthesis.
It requires relative timing c/gamma. The next section gives continuous-
time finite-rate controls and retains this concentration cost explicitly.

3. FINITE-RATE REGULARIZATION WITH A FIXED INTEGRATED ACTION BUDGET

(S,H)=(0,0), and keep the detector off. Time before the controls can be
any fixed idle interval; it changes neither coordinate.

Phase 1. Add a flip of S at rate gamma for duration A/gamma, A=ln2.

                  s'=1-2s,       h'=s-h.                   (3.1)

From zero initial means,

 s(u)=(1-exp(-2u))/2,
 h(u)=(1-exp(-u))^2/2.

At u=A this gives the exact values

                      (s_A,h_A)=(3/8,1/8),                 (3.2)

with lag d_A=s_A-h_A=1/4. The frozen-mode bank remains H=s for each
physical mode s=0 or 1; its retained S law has the correct marginal 3/8
but its averaged H mean is 3/8. It has discarded the lag.

Phase 2a: reversible SWAP control. Turn off the S-flip rate and add SWAP
at rate gamma for duration B/gamma, B=(ln2)/3. Retain the H-copy clock.
The exact mean equations are

               s'=h-s=-d,       h'=2(s-h)=2d,
                         d'=-3d.                          (3.3)

Hence

 s_end=s_A-(d_A/3)(1-exp(-3B))=1/3.                        (3.4)

The untransported frozen bank H=S predicts that a SWAP cannot change S,
so its predicted mean is still 3/8. The difference is exactly 1/24.
The integrated rate of control PROPOSALS is A+B=4ln2/3, independent of
gamma. Actual mode-changing events are no more numerous than proposals.
Each generator is a valid finite-rate classical generator for finite gamma.

Phase 2b: a single-site alternative. Instead of SWAP, copy H into S at
rate gamma for duration B/gamma, B=(ln2)/2, retaining the H-copy clock.
This changes only S; it has no simultaneous H backaction. Its equations are

               s'=h-s=-d,       h'=s-h=d,
                         d'=-2d.                          (3.5)

Therefore

 s_end=3/8-(1/4)(1-exp(-2B))/2=5/16.                       (3.6)

The frozen-mode bank again predicts 3/8, now with exact gap 1/16.
The integrated control-proposal rate is A+B=3ln2/2. The discrepancy in
subsequent full count laws is at least

 (1/16)[exp(-lambda(1-epsilon)T)
                       -exp(-lambda(1+epsilon)T)].        (3.7)

For lambda=T=1,epsilon=1/2 this is approximately 0.02396253122.
The SWAP variant gives approximately 0.01597502082.

A fixed observation horizon suffices: place the pulses after a fixed idle
time and choose the length-T observed interval immediately afterward. For
all gamma above a fixed threshold these experiments fit inside one fixed
larger horizon. Their observation budget does not grow with gamma.

The pointwise controlled S hazard during the pulses is order gamma.
The pulse durations and their timing require order 1/gamma resolution.
Their INTEGRATED hazard, even using the supremum over hidden states, is
bounded by the displayed constants. Thus an integrated-event or L1-action
budget cannot replace a gamma-independent pointwise hazard bound.
No physical actuator with uncharged bandwidth is claimed.

eta=1/128, initialize S=0 and H~Bernoulli(eta), and use the same phase

 |p_bank,eta-p_bank,0|<=eta B.                              (4.2)

Consequently

 p_bank,eta-p_actual,eta
 >=1/16-eta(1+A+2B)
 >1/16-3/128=5/128>0,                                    (4.3)
